steps.message: Standards Engineering needs the witness-test scope and scheduling package for the municipal arrays that need one, and the list of arrays the System Operations Center can be asked to release as the record stands at 07/14/2025, before the 08/15/2025 League response. The batch is covered by the municipal commissioning checklists, Checklist_Cravenwood_High.pdf through Checklist_Tresbay_Community_Center.pdf, and by the DER Program's commissioning records, including the Program Office's case tracking and its commissioning wiki. Establish which arrays are still in scope for the batch on that date. For each array in scope, determine whether the inverter or power conversion equipment actually installed there is carried on the current Certified Equipment List, and issue the package: for each array that is not carried, the tests to be performed and their basis, who performs and witnesses them, and what has to be on file first. The waiver disposition itself stays with Standards Engineering and is not yours to make. Log a scheduling item in the case tracking for each array that is not carried, record the batch determination on the case, and close the case once the arrays named in the package and the scheduling items standing on it agree. Return your work as a single Word document named Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx, filed in the Program Office's municipal commissioning folder in the document store, giving each determination with the basis you relied on, and the call made one way or the other on carriage.

ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3  ·  Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office Page 1
ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE
DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
§1  PURPOSE
This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
dispositions.
Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).
§2  SCOPE
Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.
Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.
§3  WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.
The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:
1. The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
construction.
2. Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
3. Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
4. Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
themselves listed in the body of the current edition.
Alleniom Utilities · DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com

The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model that was listed at the time
an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.
§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.
Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.
§4.3  Documentation.
The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
include, at minimum:

ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3  ·  Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office Page 1
ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE
DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
§1  PURPOSE
This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
dispositions.
Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).
§2  SCOPE
Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.
Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.
§3  WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.
The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:
1. The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
construction.
2. Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
3. Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
4. Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
themselves listed in the body of the current edition.
Alleniom Utilities · DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com

The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model that was listed at the time
an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.
§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.
Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.
§4.3  Documentation.
The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
include, at minimum:

the completed commissioning checklist, including the CEL edition identifier consulted, the CEL row
reference for each listed model, and the “waiver eligible” or “witness test required” determination;

for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated
by the Standards Engineer of record;


---

ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3  ·  Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office
Page 3

for witness-tested facilities, the witness engineer’s test record, including instrument identifiers,
measured values, pass/fail dispositions per test point, and the witness engineer’s signature and
date;

the manufacturer’s certificate of conformance, factory test report, or equivalent evidence supporting
the CEL listing relied upon;

correspondence with the customer or commissioning agent bearing on scheduling, deferrals, or
test-plan negotiation.
The commissioning record is retained in the facility interconnection file and is a prerequisite to PTO
issuance by the System Operations Center. PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed
witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination
against the current CEL edition.
End of procedure. See DIS-01 Rev 4 for interconnection standards, TCS-02 for telemetry requirements, and the
current CEL edition for the list of qualifying equipment. Revisions to this procedure are issued by Standards
Engineering and take effect on the date shown in the document-control block above.","content_type":"markdown","editor":"markdown","is_published":true,"is_private":false,"locale":"en","created_at":"2026-11-22T12:33:01.348668+00:00","updated_at":"2026-11-22T12:33:01.348668+00:00","tags":["standards","commissioning","witness-test"],"author_name":"Evan Solberg","author_email":"evan.solberg@alleniom.com"},"error":""},"isError":false}}

OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline Page 1
ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DISTRIBUTION OPERATIONS
EQUIPMENT DEPLOYMENT PRIORITIZATION
GUIDELINE
Doc no. Rev Effective Date Owner
OG-17 Rev 1 04/07/2025 Alleniom Distribution
Operations
Document Control
Supersedes: none (initial issue).
Review cycle: annual, or on material change to supplier lead times or operating criticality categories.
Approving authority: VP, Distribution Operations.
Distribution: DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; DER Planning Group; System Operations Center
(SOC); Standards Engineering; Supply Chain — Distribution Equipment.
§1  SCOPE
This guideline governs deployment sequencing of constrained utility equipment (RTUs, reclosers) across
completed sites awaiting energization. It applies to Alleniom-owned devices installed by Distribution
Operations for the purpose of energizing a construction-complete distributed energy resource (DER) site,
when supplier lead times or quarterly delivery quantities constrain the number of sites that can be
equipped in a given deployment window.
This guideline does NOT apply to application processing. Nondiscriminatory queue-order treatment of
interconnection applications is governed by Interconnection Tariff §12.7 and by the procedures
administered by Interconnection Studies; nothing in this guideline modifies, displaces, or supplements
those procedures. The rankings established under §2 operate solely on sites for which interconnection
application processing is complete, the interconnection agreement (where required) is executed, and
construction is certified complete by the customer or its contractor.
Devices out of scope: customer-owned protective equipment; utility-owned equipment already installed at
the site; distribution-system reinforcement equipment scheduled under an approved capital work order.
Program scope for the underlying DER remains as defined in DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 and Interconnection Tariff
§12.2.
§2  COMMISSIONING CRITICALITY
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA
As a general rule, deployment priority for constrained equipment follows interconnection queue order,
consistent with the nondiscriminatory treatment principles of Interconnection Tariff §12.7.
A site may be advanced ahead of queue order under certain circumstances — the urgent nature of a
request, in particular for public infrastructure (schools, hospitals, water/wastewater facilities), or an
expedited deployment pathway on reasonable customer request — but only where substantiated by the
site's own recorded attributes (per §3), in order of priority: (1) essential-service function (water/wastewater,
emergency, health); (2) committed in-service or grant-funding deadline; (3) construction-complete date.
Among sites of the same critical nature, the deciding factor is interconnection queue order; requests not
substantiated by these attributes remain in queue order.

OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline
Page 2
Factor definitions:
 Essential-service function. A site whose primary served load is a public water or wastewater facility;
a hospital, emergency-response, or first-responder facility; or a public-health facility for which loss of
service is treated as an emergency by the responsible jurisdiction. Essential-service status is
evidenced by the customer's facility classification of record and, where applicable, the served-load
designation on the interconnection application.
 Committed in-service or grant-funding deadline. A contractually committed in-service date, or a
date on which grant funding lapses if the site is not in service, established in a fully executed written
instrument between the customer and a governmental funder, project sponsor, or off-taker. Internal
customer construction targets, marketing dates, budget-cycle expectations, and school-year,
fiscal-year, or seasonal preferences do not constitute a committed deadline under this factor.
 Construction-complete date. The calendar date on which the customer's construction of the site
was certified complete and ready for utility energization steps. Where more than one date is recorded,
the earlier of (a) the customer's written notice of construction completion and (b) the utility's on-site
verification, controls.
 Queue date as tiebreaker. The interconnection queue date of the site's underlying application, used
only to break a tie among sites that rank equally on factors (1), (2), and (3).
External advocacy, correspondence volume, elected-official inquiries, and stakeholder communications
received in relation to a site do not enter the ranking. Ranking is determined from the raw attributes above,
evidenced by the source documents in §3.
§3  DOCUMENTATION
For each deployment window the DER Program Office shall assemble a deployment worksheet listing
every site meeting the eligibility conditions of §1, with the following fields drawn from the identified system
of record:
 Site name and interconnection application ID (DER Program queue).
 Customer / party of record and site service address (DER Program queue).
 Nameplate capacity and program-scope classification per DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 (application file).
 Devices required to energize (RTU, POI recloser, or both), quantities, and specification references
(Standards Engineering).
 Construction-complete date and source of certification (project construction file).
 Contracted in-service or grant-funding deadline, if any, with the executed instrument establishing it
attached by reference (customer submission).
 Essential-service classification, if any, with the customer's facility classification of record attached by
reference (application file).
 Interconnection queue date (DER Program queue).
The worksheet shall record the §2 factor on which each ranked site qualifies. Sites that do not qualify at
ranks (1) or (2) are ranked by (3) with (4) as tiebreaker. The worksheet, the ranked deployment list, and
the assigned equipment-set identifiers shall be retained in the DER Program equipment-planning file for
the applicable window and provided to the SOC concurrent with the coordination step described in §5.

documentation for a listed site, or arrival of a new site into the waiting population — shall be recorded in an

§4  VENDOR ENGAGEMENT EXPECTATIONS
Distribution Operations, working through Supply Chain, shall maintain rolling engagement with the current

 Lead-time visibility. A monthly written statement of committed lead times, next scheduled delivery

 Order coverage. Standing purchase orders shall cover no fewer than the number of device sets

data: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":43,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{"success":true,"page":{"id":48,"path":"der-program/standards/tcs-02-telemetry-comms-standard","title":"TCS-02 Telemetry Comms Standard","description":"Telemetry and Communications Standard effective 06/01/2021 requiring RTU and SCADA for sites 500 kW and above","content":"# TCS-02 Telemetry Comms Standard\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 1Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02\nALLENIOM UTILITIES — STANDARDS ENGINEERING\nTELEMETRY & COMMUNICATIONS STANDARD\nDoc no. Rev Date Owner\nTCS-02 Rev 1 06/01/2021 Alleniom Standards Engineering\nDocument title: Telemetry & Communications Standard\nApplies to: Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities interconnected to the Alleniom Utilities\ndistribution system within the DER Program scope\nEffective date: 06/01/2021\nApproving authority: Manager, Standards Engineering\n§1   PURPOSE\nThis standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time\ntelemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities\nand the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data\ncontent, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a\nDER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data\nAcquisition (SCADA) system.\nTCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited\nto telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective\nfunctions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the\nstandards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the\nscope of this document.\n§2   SCOPE\nTCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose\nnameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER\nhandled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.\nTCS-02 applies to:\n a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).\n b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).\n c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the\naggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.\n d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER\ncommissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or\ncapacity change requiring a new interconnection application.\n4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 2Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02\nWhere a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common\ncoupling with other generation, the aggregate facility is the object of this standard, and the\naggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.\n§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS\n§3.1   Ownership and installation\nEach in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)\ninstalled at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,\nowned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.\nThe customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC\nservice, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU\ninstallation drawing.\n§3.3   Functional requirements\nEach RTU shall, at minimum:\n a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station\ninstrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.\n b.   Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end\nprocessors over an approved communications path (§4).\n c.   Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum\nof seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon\nrestoration.\n d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as\ndiagnostic points.\n e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom\nSCADA/EMS Engineering only.\n§3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements\nThe RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation\ndrawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a\ndedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour\noutage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.\n§3.5   Time synchronization\nThe RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)\ntime or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a\ntimestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.\n§3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification\n§3.2   Approved models\nThe utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU\nservice: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power\nplant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the\nutility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 3\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\nPrior to the RTU being accepted as commissioned, Alleniom shall perform an end-to-end\npoint-to-point test that verifies each required data point (§6) at the SCADA operator display,\nexercises any control points released to SCADA, and validates alarm and quality flags.\nCommissioning of the RTU is a prerequisite to the telemetry condition stated in §5.\n§4   COMMUNICATIONS\n§4.1   Communications transport\nThe RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by\nSCADA/EMS Engineering:\n a.   Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or\n b.   Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or\n c.   Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held\nby Alleniom.\nCustomer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.\nWhere site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for\ninterconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.\n§4.2   SCADA protocol\nThe RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Secure\nAuthentication v5 shall be enabled on the DNP3 link where supported by the RTU. Configuration\nparameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —\nshall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.\n§4.3   Availability\nThe end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a\nmonthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Persistent\nloss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis and shall be\ncorrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected\nequipment.\n§4.4   Address and IP management\nAll IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and\nAlleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate\nconnections toward the RTU other than as expressly permitted in the site-specific configuration\nrecord.\n§5   TELEMETRY CONDITION FOR PERMISSION TO OPERATE\n§5.   ≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry.\nThis requirement applies to all in-scope DER sites, including aggregated facilities under\nDIS-01 §3.4.\nLive telemetry, for the purposes of §5, means that the RTU installed under §3 is:\n a.   Physically installed, configured, and end-to-end commissioned in accordance with §3.6;\n\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 4\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\n b.   Communicating with Alleniom SCADA over an approved transport (§4) at the refresh\ncadence required by §6; and\n c.   Presenting all required data points (§6) as valid (not stale, not forced, not flagged\nbad-quality) at the SCADA operator display at the moment Permission to Operate (PTO) is\nissued.\nCompliance with §5 is confirmed by the SOC Shift Supervisor on shift at the time PTO is\nrequested. The SOC's confirmation is recorded against the interconnection file. PTO shall not be\nissued to any in-scope DER site until §5 is satisfied.\n§6   DATA POINTS AND REFRESH RATES\n§6.1   Required data points\nEach in-scope DER site shall present, at minimum, the following analog and status points to\nAlleniom SCADA. Where the site's arrangement includes multiple inverter blocks or multiple\naggregated facilities behind a common POI, values shall be reported both individually per block\nand as a facility total.\nAnalog values (per site, and per block where applicable):\nPoint\nUnits\nSign convention\nReal power, net export at POI\nkW\nExport positive\nReactive power, net at POI\nkVAr\nAbsorbing positive\nPOI voltage, per phase\nV\n—\nPOI current, per phase\nA\n—\nFrequency at POI\nHz\n—\nGross generation (per inverter block)\nkW\nGeneration positive\nAuxiliary/parasitic load (where separately metered)\nkW\nLoad positive\nCumulative energy delivered\nkWh\nExport positive\nCumulative energy received\nkWh\nImport positive\nAmbient / cabinet temperature (RTU health)\n°C\n—\nStatus and diagnostic points:\nPoint\nDescription\nSite online / offline\nAggregate operating state of the DER\nInverter/PCS block status\nPer block: run, standby, fault\nCommunications heartbeat\nRTU-to-SCADA path health\nTime-sync quality\nGNSS/NTP discipline status\nConfiguration version\nActive RTU configuration identifier\nAlarm summary\nRolled-up device alarm state\n§6.2   Refresh rates\n\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 5\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\nAnalog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3\nClass 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than\nevery sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an\nintegrity poll no less frequently than every sixty (60) seconds. Cumulative energy registers shall be\nreported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.\n§6.3   Data quality\nEvery value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,\nrestart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the\nRTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be\nreported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.\n§6.4   Retention\nAlleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six\n(36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,\nengineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.\n§7   CYBERSECURITY\n§7.1   Applicability\nThe RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any\ncustomer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this\nsection. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security\nprogram consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.\n§7.2   Access control\nLocal and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to\nAlleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication\nagainst Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are\nmanaged by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.\n§7.3   Communications security\nDNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. §1   PURPOSE
This standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time
telemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities
and the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data
content, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a
DER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) system.
TCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited
to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
scope of this document.
§2   SCOPE
TCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose
nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.
TCS-02 applies to:
 a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).
 b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).
 c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the
aggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.
 d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.

PURPOSE\nDPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources\n(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault\nclearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the\nutility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to\nthe distribution network.\nThis standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective\ndevices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards\nEngineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope\nprojects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.\n2. SCOPE\nThis standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service\nterritory, including but not limited to:\n1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).\n2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).\n3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to\nthe distribution system through the point of common coupling.\nSub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this\nstandard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall\napply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.\nNon-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any\noperating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection\nguidance.\n3. REFERENCES\nThe following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:\n IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with\nAssociated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.\n IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.\n IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible\nAutomatic Circuit Reclosers.\n ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.\n\n\n---\n\nDPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023 Page 2\n Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.\n Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.\n4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS\n4.1 General\nEvery distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment\nsufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:\n(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility\nreclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.\n(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on\nthe utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection\nstandard.\n(c)Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption\nbetween the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.\n(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is\ncleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary\ntripping of either.\n4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement\nEvery export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection\n(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.\nThe POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:\n1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,\ncurrent and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and\noperated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary\nconductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications\nbackhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.\n2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit\ninterrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per\nDistribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.\n3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,\nwith settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:\n— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),\n— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,\n— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,\n— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,\n— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power\nbackstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,\n— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.\n4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the\ncontrol cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of\ncommunications shall not defeat local protection.\nWhere a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering\ndetermination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.\n\n---\n\nDPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023\nPage 3\n5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect\noperable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of\nclearance holds.\n6. Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location\naccessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer\npremises.\n4.3 DER-Side Protection\nDER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection\nprotection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI\nrecloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.\nDER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.\n4.4 Grounding\nThe DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with\nthe grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's\ngrounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.\n4.5 Anti-Islanding\nThe DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone\nrequirements of the applicable interconnection standard. 1. PURPOSE
DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
the distribution network.
This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.
2. SCOPE
This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
territory, including but not limited to:
1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
guidance.
3. REFERENCES
The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
 IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
 IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
 IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
 ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.

4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c)Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),

— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,

— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.

SUBJECT:	Backlog Review — Commercial DER Interconnection Program
The Alleron Municipal League's letter of 06/20/2025, submitted on behalf of fourteen member municipalities and school districts and copied to the APUC Energy Resources Division, is the trigger. We are not going to litigate its tone. We are going to fix the underlying condition that produced it.
Effective immediately, I am ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. The scope covers the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population — every application currently sitting in the program queue. I want each one accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action.
The following non-negotiable dates govern this work:
1. 08/15/2025 — Formal written response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs owns the response letter. Harriet Ngoyi is the signatory. The response must address the League's five enumerated requests substantively and by project, not in aggregate.

Ground rules for every disposition reached in this review:
Every disposition must be tariff-defensible. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, or operating guideline that supports the action. If the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready.
Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as they are written. Do not shortcut them, and do not extend them beyond what the tariff contemplates.
Where standards or procedural conflicts exist, route them through the established referral process. Do not resolve them informally in the queue.
No interim energization, no political prioritization, and no queue-date inheritance outside of what the tariff and program policy permit.
Reporting cadence. I want weekly progress updates to the VP office, in writing, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025. Format: counts by disposition category, exceptions requiring VP attention, and any item at risk of missing the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates. Meera, Ivo, and Marcus will support the DER Program Manager with the data pulls, study status, and telemetry/equipment inputs their groups own.
Escalate obstacles to me directly. I would rather field a problem on a Tuesday than read about it in a League follow-up letter.
/s/
Dana Whitcomb
Vice President, Distribution Operations
Alleniom Utilities

**From:** Rosa Camarena <rosa.camarena@brookfenusd.org>
**To:** der.program@alleniom.com
**Date:** Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:42:18 -0500
**Subject:** Urgent: school array energization priority
**Cc:** Dana Whitcomb <dana.whitcomb@alleniom.com>, Harriet Ngoyi <harriet.ngoyi@alleniom.com>

---

To the DER Program Office:

I am writing again — and I want to be direct about the fact that this is not the first, second, or third time I have raised this with your office — to ask for a firm answer on when Alleniom Utilities intends to energize the two solar arrays serving Brookfen Unified School District. This message is dated 06/30/2025 and I would like a written response before the end of next week.

The two arrays in question, and their status on our side, are as follows:

  • Brookfen North High School Array — 720 kW. Construction was declared complete by our contractor on 04/18/2025. The local electrical inspector closed out the installation the same week. The system has been standing idle, energized-ready, for more than ten weeks.

  • Brookfen West Elementary Array — 640 kW. Construction was declared complete on 05/23/2025. Inspection was closed out shortly thereafter. This system has now been standing idle for over a month.

Neither array has been energized. Neither array has a firm energization date on record with the District. Each time our office contacts your program inbox we are told that a component — variously described as a "telemetry unit" or an "RTU" — has not yet been delivered by your supplier, and that we are somewhere in a queue behind other sites. What we have never been given, in writing, is the position of our sites in that queue, the identity of the sites ahead of us, or the basis on which those sites are being served ahead of ours.

I have to tell you plainly that the patience of the Brookfen school board and the District's superintendent is exhausted. The 2025–2026 school year begins for our students on 08/26/2025. Both of these arrays were financed, in significant part, on the strength of first-year operating-cost savings that were built into the District's adopted budget for that same school year and presented to our board and to the community at public meetings. Every additional week that these systems sit dark is a week of budgeted savings the District will not realize and will have to explain to the board, to our parents, and to the taxpayers of Brookfen who approved the underlying bond measure. Our high school's building-systems curriculum was also structured around students being able to observe the array in operation from the beginning of the term; that piece of the school year is now at risk of slipping into the second semester or being cut altogether.

You will by now have received the Alleron Municipal League's letter of 06/20/2025, signed by Executive Director Alden Pryce, escalating this same set of concerns on behalf of the District and thirteen other League members. Brookfen USD is one of the members named in that letter and stands fully behind the requests it contains. This message is not a substitute for the League's letter; it is intended to make the District's individual position, and the specifics of our two sites, unmistakable to your office.

What I am asking for, directly, is this: in the next allocation of the equipment your program office is holding up as the constraint — the RTU / telemetry units your staff have referenced in prior calls — I am asking Alleniom Utilities to advance the District's two waiting arrays ahead of the other sites presently competing for those units. Brookfen North completed construction on 04/18/2025 and Brookfen West on 05/23/2025. Both are public school facilities. Both have children returning to the building in eight weeks. Neither array can wait for a second or third delivery cycle without meaningful harm to the District's fiscal position and to the educational program these systems were installed to support.

If there is a formal process for requesting that our two sites be advanced in your next equipment allocation, please tell me what that process is and I will follow it today. If there is not, please treat this message as our written request under whatever mechanism your program uses to weigh these decisions, and please confirm receipt.

I am copying Ms. Whitcomb and Ms. Ngoyi so that this request is on the record with senior distribution operations and regulatory affairs, and so that no one at your program office is later in a position to say the District did not put this in writing in time.

I would like a written reply — not a call-back, a written reply — by close of business Friday, 07/11/2025. Silence past that date will require the District to raise this matter again through the League and, if necessary, directly with the Commission's Energy Resources Division, whose staff we understand is already tracking this program.

I am available at (612) 448-0311 during District business hours if it would help to talk any of this through. I would strongly prefer to resolve it with your office.

Regards,

Rosa Camarena
Facilities Director
Brookfen Unified School District
1725 Grantway Drive, Brookfen, Alleron 12BR
(612) 448-0311

Commercial & Industrial Photovoltaic Contracting
Office (612) 555-0733 · Alleron Electrical Contractor Lic. #EC-11847
DER COMMISSIONING CERTIFICATE
Document: NGSS-COM-2017-0348
Issued: 09/28/2017
Project Identification
Site Name Merrow Creamery Legacy PV
Site Address
Customer Merrow Creamery
Utility Alleniom Utilities
Nameplate Capacity 800 kW
Commissioning Date 09/28/2017
Contractor of Record Northern Grid Solar Services
NGSS Project No. NGSS-2017-118
System Description
Rooftop-mounted photovoltaic generating facility connected behind the existing customer service meter at the Merrow
Creamery dairy processing plant. Array totals 800 kW nameplate AC, distributed across the north and south
production-building roof planes. Three-phase, 480 V output tied into the customer's existing 480 V main distribution
switchboard via a dedicated PV feeder breaker; no modifications to the utility service entrance conductors or the
revenue meter. Generation is intended to offset on-site process load; no export-focused equipment installed.
Modules: 2,580 × 310 W crystalline-silicon PV modules, mounted on ballasted low-tilt racking.
Inverters: 8 × 100 kW three-phase string inverters (UL 1741 listed; IEEE 1547 anti-islanding).
AC combining: 800 A PV subpanel feeding a 1,000 A PV feeder breaker in the existing 480 V main switchboard.
Point of common coupling: Load side of the existing utility service meter.

schedule

9 Voltage and frequency trip settings verified Pass Per approved settings sheet
10 Grounding electrode conductor and equipment bondingPass Per NEC 690 / 250
11 Ground-fault detection (GFDI) function test Pass All inverters

Interconnection
Interconnection agreement executed with Alleniom Utilities on 08/14/2017 under the utility's small-generator
interconnection procedures then in effect. System operates in parallel with the utility service behind the existing
service meter; the facility is not configured for scheduled export operation and no additional utility-owned protective,
monitoring, or communications equipment is installed at the point of common coupling.

Site: 80 Old Mill Road, Holcott, Alleron 84HO. Nameplate 510 kW AC; POI utility secondary, service transformer T-4. DER class: Commercial small-scale (500 kW–1 MW). Checklist CX-HOL-LIB-01, Rev 0, 06/17/2025.\n\n**Installed inverter (as commissioned):** Selvix SV-720 (cover sheet; footnote ¹).\n\n**Why a witness test is required:** The installed inverter is **not carried on the current Certified Equipment List, CEL-2025-Q2** (published 04/30/2025; Doc no. CEL-2025-Q2). No “Selvix” model appears on the CEL-2025-Q2 Inverters or Power Control Systems tabs. The checklist footnote cites only the SUPERSEDED edition — “Selvix SV-720 listed in CEL-2024-Q4 (published 10/31/2024)” — and that listing was not carried forward into CEL-2025-Q2 (confirmed against the superseded workbook: Selvix SV-720, 720 kW, UL 1741-SB, 10/31/2024, “Initial listing this edition”). Under the Witness Test & Waiver Procedure (ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3) §3 (corollaries 3 and 5) and §4.1, a listing that appeared solely on a superseded CEL edition confers no waiver eligibility once the successor edition (CEL-2025-Q2, effective 04/30/2025) takes effect; the facility is ineligible for a waiver and an on-site witness test is required before PTO. The checklist’s “witness test: waiver eligible” mark is overridden by the current-CEL lookup.\n\n**Tests to be performed (basis):** Per ENG-PRC-014 §4.2, testing per IEEE 1547.1, including at minimum: (a) protective-function trip tests (27/59, 81U/81O, 25, 32 as configured) against the approved settings sheet; (b) anti-islanding function test (IEEE 1547.1); (c) voltage and frequency ride-through verifications per DIS-01 Rev 4 §6 (Category II). Basis: ENG-PRC-014 §4.2; IEEE 1547.1; DIS-01 Rev 4 §6; approved protection settings sheet / coordination study on file.\n\n**Who performs / witnesses:** Performed by the customer (Town of Holcott) or its commissioning agent (Alleniom Field Services Crew 12; field engineer M. Halbrook, P.E., AFE-1042) with qualified personnel, calibrated instrumentation, and the approved test plan (ENG-PRC-014 §4.2). Witnessed by an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer — independent of the commissioning agent of record — assigned by Standards Engineering, who records measured values and pass/fail per test point and dispositions the test (ENG-PRC-014 §4.2–§4.3). Scheduled by the DER Program Office commissioning coordinator.\n\n**What must be on file first (prerequisites to PTO):**\n1. Completed commissioning checklist marked “witness test required” with the CEL edition consulted (CEL-2025-Q2) and the finding that Selvix SV-720 is not carried — Sections A–D already Pass on file (06/17/2025).\n2. Approved protection settings sheet / coordination study (checklist Section B).\n3. Customer/commissioning-agent test plan, calibrated-instrumentation list with current calibration certificates, and qualified-personnel designation.\n4. [body.p.54]: **Determination — not carried; witness test required.[size=10.5]**
[body.p.55]: The installed inverter Selvix SV-720 is not carried on the current Certified Equipment List, CEL-2025-Q2 (published 04/30/2025). No “Selvix” model appears on the CEL-2025-Q2 Inverters or Power Control Systems tabs. The checklist footnote cites only the SUPERSEDED edition — “Selvix SV-720 listed in CEL-2024-Q4 (published 10/31/2024)” — and that listing was not carried forward into CEL-2025-Q2 (confirmed against the superseded workbook: Selvix SV-720, 720 kW, UL 1741-SB, 10/31/2024, “Initial listing this edition”). Under ENG-PRC-014 §3 (corollaries 3 and 5) and §4.1, a listing that appeared solely on a superseded CEL edition confers no waiver eligibility once the successor edition (CEL-2025-Q2, effective 04/30/2025) takes effect; the facility is ineligible for a waiver and an on-site witness test is required before PTO. The checklist’s “witness test: waiver eligible” mark is overridden by the current-CEL lookup.[size=10.5]

[body.p.59] (style=List Bullet): Voltage and frequency ride-through verifications per DIS-01 Rev 4 §6 (Category II) and the approved settings sheet.
[body.p.60] (style=List Bullet): Basis: ENG-PRC-014 §4.2; IEEE 1547.1; DIS-01 Rev 4 §6; approved protection settings sheet / protection coordination study on file.

[body.p.62] (style=List Bullet): Performed by the customer (Town of Holcott) or its commissioning agent (Alleniom Field Services Crew 12; field engineer M. Halbrook, P.E., AFE-1042), supplying the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and qualified personnel (ENG-PRC-014 §4.2).

[body.p.69] (style=List Number): Witness engineer’s signed test record — instrument IDs, measured values, pass/fail per test point, signature, and date — produced at the test (§4.3).
[body.p.70] (style=List Number): Live telemetry to the SOC per TCS-02 §5 (utility-owned RTU installed and SCADA verified end-to-end). **Installed inverter (as commissioned):** Arvexa PV-750 (cover sheet; factory profile per Section 2).

**Why a witness test is required:** The installed inverter is **not carried on the current Certified Equipment List, CEL-2025-Q2** (published 04/30/2025; Doc no. CEL-2025-Q2). No “Arvexa” model appears on the CEL-2025-Q2 Inverters tab or the Power Control Systems tab, and none appeared on the superseded CEL-2024-Q4. Under the Witness Test & Waiver Procedure (ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3) §3 and §4.1, an inverter not present in the body of the current CEL edition makes the facility ineligible for a witness-test waiver; an on-site witness test is required before PTO. 3. Customer/commissioning-agent test plan, calibrated-instrumentation list with current calibration certificates, and qualified-personnel designation.
4. Witness engineer’s signed test record (instrument IDs, measured values, pass/fail per test point, signature, date) — produced at the test.
5. Live telemetry to the SOC per TCS-02 §5 (utility-owned RTU installed and SCADA verified end-to-end). **NOTE:** Darnwick telemetry is PENDING — RTU allocation not yet scheduled (checklist Section 5); must close before PTO (SOC will not release without it).

PTO shall not be issued until both the signed witness-test disposition (item 4) and live telemetry (item 5) are on file (ENG-PRC-014 §4.3; TCS-02 §5). On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date (ENG-PRC-014 §4.2).

[body.p.6]: This package responds to Standards Engineering’s request under the DER Program backlog review. It does three things, and only three things, for the municipal commissioning batch:[size=10.5]
[body.p.7] (style=List Number): **Establish scope — **it establishes which municipal arrays are still in the witness-test batch as of the 07/14/2025 record date;
[body.p.8] (style=List Number): **Determine carriage — **for each array still in scope, it determines whether the inverter or power-conversion equipment actually installed there is carried on the current Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2), and records the call one way or the other with its basis; and
[body.p.9] (style=List Number): **Issue the package — **for each array that is not carried, it issues the witness-test scope and scheduling package — the tests to be performed and their basis, who performs and who witnesses them, and what must be on file first.
[body.p.10]: *It also gives, for the same record date, the list of arrays the System Operations Center (SOC) can be asked to release.[size=10.5]*
[body.p.11]: **The waiver disposition itself stays with Standards Engineering and is not made in this package. A positive carriage (waiver-eligibility) determination is, per the governing procedure, a necessary but not sufficient condition for a waiver; the written waiver disposition is reserved to Standards Engineering.[size=10.5]**

steps.message:
All deliverables are on disk, verified to open correctly, and improved. Work complete.

## Summary

**Deliverable — Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx**, filed in the Program Office's municipal commissioning folder in the document store at the exact path the instruction gives (verified present in both the local document store and the Nextcloud document store, 48,051 bytes, opens correctly with 12 headings, header/footer with page numbers, document properties set):
- `/filesystem/Commissioning/Municipal/Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx`
- `/DER_Program/Commissioning/Municipal/Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx`

It gives each determination with the basis relied on and the carriage call one way or the other:
- **Scope (07/14/2025):** 5 of 6 arrays in scope — Cravenwood, Darnwick, Holcott, Lockmere, Marden Falls; Tresbay withdrew 07/09/2025 and is out.
- **CEL-2025-Q2 carriage:** Carried (waiver-eligible, disposition reserved to Standards Engineering) — Cravenwood (Solmery SM-215K-3P), Lockmere (Torvane TE-180K), Marden Falls (Solmery SM-245K-3P). Not carried → witness test required — Darnwick (Arvexa PV-750, never listed) and Holcott (Selvix SV-720, only on superseded CEL-2024-Q4). Basis: ENG-PRC-014 §3/§4.1.
- **Witness-test package (§5, the two not-carried arrays):** tests + basis (IEEE 1547.1 / DIS-01 §6 / ENG-PRC-014 §4.2), who performs (customer/commissioning agent) vs. who witnesses (independent Alleniom witness engineer assigned by Standards Engineering), and the prerequisites that must be on file first (incl. live telemetry per TCS-02 §5 before PTO).
- **SOC release list (07/14/2025):** Lockmere and Marden Falls (telemetry live; only the waiver disposition remains); the other three cannot be released.

Supporting work in the case tracking (OpenProject "DER Program Backlog Review"): batch determination recorded on **WP #45 (Closed)**; scheduling items **WP #47 (Holcott, Open)** and **WP #48 (Darnwick, Open)** assigned to Evan Solberg — the arrays named in the package and the scheduling items standing on the case agree (2 = 2). The waiver disposition was left to Standards Engineering as instructed.
